greeting.speaker: Sedge the Bird Archer
text: Sit where you like. Everyone who comes in wet sits by the bell, and everyone who comes in armed sits by the door. You're both, so choose.
Careful of the boards by the water. They're older than the village and prouder than the priest.
Don't stand between me and the reeds. Nothing personal — I've lost two dinners that way this week.

options.text: What does the bell ring for?
The fen's been picked over. Somebody's been through here already.

again.speaker: Sedge the Bird Archer
text: You know where to sit now. That's most of belonging, out here.
The water's up since you were last through. So is everything that lives in it.
I heard a version of you before I saw you. It had more horses.

options.text: What's come out of the reeds since?
Those riders. Did they come back?
Ale for the room, and keep the change.

the_door.speaker: Sedge the Bird Archer
the_door.text: Sensible. The bell rings for the water and I'd not want it ringing behind you.

the_bow.speaker: Sedge the Bird Archer
the_bow.text: Hunger did. Fowl won't wait for a second arrow and neither will anything walking out of the reeds.

the_round.speaker: Sedge the Bird Archer
the_round.text: Then you'll get names, and names travel further out here than coin does.

she_admits_it.speaker: Sedge the Bird Archer
she_admits_it.text: Riders. Two weeks back. Took the smoked eel and left the traps, which means they weren't hungry, which is worse.

she_deflects.speaker: Sedge the Bird Archer
she_deflects.text: The fen picks itself over. Ask the water what it took, if you've got the afternoon.

the_bell.speaker: Sedge the Bird Archer
the_bell.text: Water coming up, or something coming in. Same rope, different number of pulls. Learn the difference before you sleep here.

the_reeds_since.speaker: Sedge the Bird Archer
text: A boat with nobody in it and the oars still shipped. I burnt it. Don't ask me why.
Birds going up at dusk with nothing under them. Three nights running.
Less than usual, and that's the part I don't like.

the_riders_again.speaker: Sedge the Bird Archer
the_riders_again.text: Once. They looked at the bell rope and rode on. Whoever sent them wanted us counted, not robbed.
